mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant deviation from zero during high-rate regimes (p > 0.05 in t-test), or the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, investors anticipate a pre-emptive rate hike by the Fed, causing a short-term discounting effect that lowers S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods when CPIAUCSL > 3% for >2 months, SPX 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or the inflation signal is spurious (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, prompting equity valuation expansion and higher S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% in a month while UNRATE decreases by >0.5 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In strong labor market regimes, the 5-day forward return is not significantly higher than the 30-day historical average (p > 0.05), or the PAYEMS/UNRATE relationship is not statistically significant (R² < 0.3).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months indicates resilient consumer demand, which lowers discount rates and supports positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 3 months of strong HOUST growth, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect is explained by other variables (multivariate F-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month is interpreted as a supply shock that raises uncertainty, prompting risk-off flows and negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in a single month
failure_condition: During significant INDPRO contractions, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the shock is not confirmed by other supply indicators (e.g., no simultaneous spike in Durable Goods).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of RSAFS exceeds 7,000 million dollars, it reflects elevated financial system liquidity, which lowers real interest rates and supports positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
regime_hint: high liquidity conditions in financial markets
failure_condition: In high-RSAFS liquidity regimes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the liquidity signal is not confirmed by other liquidity indicators (e.g., no correlation with M2 growth).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) and a rise in labor force participation (PAYEMS) suggests a demographic or policy shift that boosts labor supply, lowering discount rates and producing positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2% while PAYEMS increases by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: During labor-supply expansion, the 5-day forward return is not significantly positive (p > 0.05), or the UNRATE/PAYEMS relationship is not robust (Granger causality fails).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in consumer confidence (indirect proxy via a sharp one-month decline in HOUST) combined with a rising UNRATE suggests a demand softening, which raises discount rates and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by >10% in a month while UNRATE rises by >0.3 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: During demand-softening regimes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.05), or the HOUST/UNRATE interaction is not statistically significant (F-test p > 0.1).
